I farm the same 10.1 mu in a wheat-maize rotation, so I will plant 10.1 mu of wheat and then the same 10.1 mu of maize after wheat harvest. I have done this for many years, so I do not start from zero. I look first at what worked before, then I adjust a little. On my land, if fertilizer is too short, the crop shows it fast, and then it is hard to make up yield later. Fertilizer costs money, but losing grain costs more, so I will keep the rate a bit on the safe side. Since I have well irrigation, I will use water at the key times instead of gambling on rain. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough base fertilizer, then topdress nitrogen when the crop starts to stand up strong in spring. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, give enough fertilizer early, and then add more nitrogen around jointing. I will not do anything too fancy. I will follow the way that has worked in our area, keep the field clean, water on time, spray when I see disease or insects likely to come, and aim for steady yield more than risky saving.
